📌 Token Vesting: Why Team and Investor Tokens Unlock Over Time

Main Points
⏺ Token vesting schedules control when founders, teams, and investors can claim their tokens
⏺ Unlocks are usually spread over months or years with cliffs and linear releases
⏺ This post explains how vesting protects projects from instant dump pressure

1️⃣ What Is Vesting — tokens reserved for insiders are locked and only become claimable at set dates
2️⃣ Cliff Period — an initial lockup (for example, 6–12 months) where no tokens unlock at all
3️⃣ Linear Unlock — after the cliff, tokens are released gradually, such as monthly over several years
4️⃣ Market Impact — large unlocks can increase sell pressure, so traders often track vesting calendars
5️⃣ Trust Signal — transparent vesting shows that core contributors are aligned for the long term, not just a quick exit

Final Thoughts

Token vesting turns insider allocations into a time-based commitment — the longer they’re locked in, the more skin in the game the project really has.

📌 Bitcoin price stalls near $82K as key resistance holds 

🌐 Bitcoin price pulled back after briefly breaking above $82,000 on Sept. 4, as traders took profits following a short squeeze driven by softer Federal Reserve expectations and renewed demand for US spot Bitcoin ETFs. According to data from cryptonews, Bitcoin price traded near $81,150 at the time of writing, having failed to hold an intraday move above the $82,000 psychological level. The pullback left the asset about 1% below its local high but still well above the $80,000 mark reclaimed during the previous session. 

⚠️ The rally accelerated after Bitcoin moved out of a range around $77,000–$79,000. Short sellers were forced to close leveraged positions as the price crossed $80,000, adding automatic buy orders to the market. CoinGlass data cited by market reports showed that the broader crypto market recorded more than $500 million in liquidations during the rally, with short positions accounting for most of the total. Bitcoin shorts reportedly absorbed about $415 million of those losses.

📊 Price action has since slowed near a technically important area. Galaxy Research data shared by analyst Quinten François placed Bitcoin’s 50-week moving average near $81,041, almost level with the current market price. According to François, Bitcoin has not closed a weekly candle above that moving average since November 2025. He said a move through $82,800 would also produce the first higher high of the broader downtrend and bring $90,000 back into consideration.

This is a very interesting concept for building, something I'm always interested in as that was my profession at one time...

I also am in love with any new technologies that are smarter, working less harder, are more sustainable and help free humanity's most valuable currency which is time!

The strategy behind systems like TRIQBRIQ is to trade materials for time. On a macro level, the cost dynamic shakes out like this:

🔴The Material Premium: 
You are purchasing highly engineered, precision-milled timber blocks rather than mass-produced, cheap 2x4 studs. This makes your initial material package significantly more expensive than standard framing lumber.

🔴The Labor & Time Collapse: 
Traditional framing requires weeks of specialized carpenter labor, followed by separate multi-day processes for exterior sheathing, house wrap, insulation installation, drywall hanging, and exterior siding. With the interlocking block method, a small crew of standard laborers can stack the entire shell of a house in less than three days, completely bypassing all those middle steps and specialized crews.

When you add the costs together, the net price to build the structural shell lands very close to conventional construction. 

However, because the building is closed in weeks ahead of schedule, you save thousands in soft construction costs such as builder risk insurance, equipment rentals (like scaffolding), and construction loan interest fees. 

Ultimately, you get a premium, incredibly sustainable solid-wood structure in a fraction of the time for a comparable overall price.

Many people complain that new technologies, including robotics, will put people out of work and steal their jobs. 

From my own experience as a builder for 20 years, the biggest challenge we faced was finding people who wanted to work and had a strong work ethic. 

The second major challenge was the weather, followed by the extra costs these first two issues added to every project. That doesn’t even account for the expenses tied to insurance and interest fees. And when an accident does happen, it’s like pulling teeth to get the insurance companies to cover the losses, despite the premiums you’ve paid for years. 

To me, these new technologies sidestep all of those headaches.I’m sure people in the past feared new technologies just as many do now. Yet we’re entering a revolution in how things get done, one unlike anything the world has seen before. 

The freedom it will bring is something people have only dreamed of.👈

📣 A hacker associated with the third wave of Coldcard wallet thefts began converting stolen Bitcoin into Ether through THORChain on Sept. 3, according to Galaxy Research’s Alex Thorn.
